chunks: (3) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran narrated from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying:
"The Master of this Command has two occultations." And I heard him say: "The Qa'im will rise while there is no homage on the neck of anyone."

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations and the condition of the Imam's rise according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the doctrine of the two occultations—Minor (al-Ghaybah al-Sughra) and Major (al-Ghaybah al-Kubra)—establishing the theological framework for the Twelfth Imam's hidden presence. Furthermore, he clarifies that the Imam's ultimate rise to global justice occurs independently, without requiring prior allegiance (bay'ah) to any preceding political authority, a key distinction in Shia eschatology regarding the legitimacy of the Mahdi's rule.
